summary: First-finish smoke test. Backend public endpoints, auth session injection, admin CRUD, settings, order approve/reject/complete, stats, admins allowlist all working. Frontend home + admin login pages load correctly with 7 categories and hero. One HIGH severity blocker found: POST /api/orders returns 500 even though the order is persisted — response cannot be serialized due to MongoDB ObjectId injection into the doc after insert_one. This breaks the entire client checkout flow (Checkout.jsx will not receive the created order and cannot redirect to /confirmation/{order_number}).
passed: GET /api/categories returns 7 seeded categories (PUBG Mobile, Free Fire, eFootball, DLS, FC Mobile, CapCut Pro, Autres)
GET /api/settings/public returns margin_percent=10 and all default fields
GET /api/auth/me without cookie returns 401; with injected Bearer token returns super_admin torrepablo7040@gmail.com
POST /api/admin/products creates product; GET /api/products returns price = base_price * (1 + margin/100) [100 -> 110 at 10%]
Order (created despite 500 response) carries payment_beneficiary_name/payment_receiver_number from settings and total_amount = unit_price * qty (110 * 2 = 220 correct)
POST /api/admin/orders/{id}/approve|reject|complete correctly transitions status; reject stores rejection_reason
GET /api/admin/stats returns total_orders, pending, approved, rejected, completed, revenue, products, customers
Frontend home page renders hero + all 7 categories + navigation
Frontend /admin/login renders 'Se connecter avec Google' button

failed.issue: Endpoint returns HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error' although the order IS inserted in MongoDB. Root cause: after `await db.orders.insert_one(doc)` in create_order (server.py ~line 408), motor mutates `doc` in-place by adding `_id: ObjectId`. FastAPI then tries to serialize `doc` and fails with: ValueError: [TypeError("'ObjectId' object is not iterable"), TypeError('vars() argument must have __dict__ attribute')]. This blocks the customer checkout redirect to /confirmation/{order_number}.
failed.evidence: Backend log: 'POST /api/orders HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error'. Traceback in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log ends with 'ValueError: [TypeError("ObjectId object is not iterable"), TypeError(vars() argument must have __dict__ attribute)]'. Confirmed via curl: response body 'Internal Server Error' with HTTP 500, then GET /api/orders/lookup returns the persisted order (order_number FT-XXXXXXXX, status=pending, total=220, unit=110).

action_items: Fix create_order in /app/backend/server.py: return `order.model_dump()` (built before insert) instead of the mutated `doc`, OR explicitly strip `_id` after insert (e.g. `doc.pop('_id', None)` before returning). Same defensive pattern should be considered for any other endpoint that returns a doc right after insert_one.
